status: Resolved — source repair, sealed runner publication, and clean-install adoption verified; formal closeout remains
area: A malformed skill template is dropped from every install profile with no diagnostic
finding: parseSkillTemplate accepts any YAML frontmatter. A template file that carries built-SKILL frontmatter (name/description/argument-hint) instead of the atm.skillTemplate contract (schemaId/id/title/summary/tier/installProfiles) parses without error and is counted by loadSkillTemplates, but its frontmatter.id, tier and installProfiles are all undefined, so skillBelongsToProfile returns false for every profile and loadSkillTemplatesForProfile drops it. No adapter ever projects it, and nothing reports that a source template produced no output. The whole chain then agrees: the baker emits nothing, npm run validate:skill-templates reports ok because it validates the templates it loaded rather than asserting each source file reached a profile, and integration verify reports ok because it compares installed files against baked files and both sides are equally missing the skill. The result is a source template that exists, is readable, looks correct to a human, and simply does not exist for any agent.
expectedBehavior: A source file under templates/skills that fails to satisfy the atm.skillTemplate contract must be a hard validation failure naming the file and the missing fields, not a silent profile-filter miss. Corpus completeness is the invariant worth enforcing: every *.skill.md in the source root must project into at least one install profile, and a template that reaches zero profiles must fail validate:skill-templates. integration verify must not be able to report ok for a corpus whose source count and projected count disagree, because agreement between two equally empty sides is not evidence of correctness.
evidenceOrRepro: 2026-08-14, ATM-FRAMEWORK-TEMP-claude-008-gov-0366. templates/skills/atm-framework-quickfix.skill.md carried built-SKILL frontmatter, so .claude/skills/atm-framework-quickfix/SKILL.md was never generated while integration verify claude-code reported ok and npm run validate:skill-templates reported ok over 18 source templates. Measured directly against packages/integrations-core/src/compiler/skill-templates.ts with two source roots identical except for that one file's frontmatter: with the repaired frontmatter, loadSkillCorpusSourceSnapshot reports templateCount 25 and loadSkillTemplatesForProfile('framework-full') returns 25 ids including atm-framework-quickfix; with the malformed frontmatter, templateCount is still 25 while framework-full returns 24 and does not include it. templateCount is therefore not a completeness signal — the file is counted as loaded and lost one step later at the profile filter, which is why no count anywhere looked wrong. ignoredSourceTemplatePaths was [] in both cases and did not report the loss. Repaired by 9d12aeb5276df38ef25feb5345a5bc7768732ef3, which rewrites only that file's frontmatter and leaves its body byte-identical; the baked .claude output regenerated from the baker with a body identical to .agents/skills/atm-framework-quickfix/SKILL.md.
followUp: Source coverage repair landed in 9b2e18c936ba801499eb103ab49c55e5223146ea. Static integration adapters expose an independent sourceFileCount contract, and integration verify fails closed with source-coverage-mismatch when the source corpus is larger than the current projection; regression coverage is in tests/cli/integration-source-coverage-parity.test.ts. Sealed runner publication is verified at de42d56ce2bdc6ee4f876c657006542e830adf72. Fresh validate-npm-clean-install passed with skeletonPackages=27, publishedPackages=[@ai-atomic-framework/cli], isolatedInstall=true, and adoptionVerified=true. Focused source tests, typecheck, integration parity, six-editor parity, encoding guard, and clean-install adoption pass. Remaining item is formal governance closeout only.
